data.title: CCTV4：Documentary 'OUR HOME, OUR YANGTZE' to Premiere Soon
data.description:
CCTV4：Documentary 'OUR HOME, OUR YANGTZE' to Premiere Soon

CCTV4：Documentary 'OUR HOME, OUR YANGTZE' to Premiere Soon

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Across four episodes, Our Home, Our Yangtze tells a decade of change along the Yangtze River Economic Belt through four unusual narrators: a fish, a single kilowatt-hour of electricity, a microchip and a shipping container. Their stories explore ecological conservation, industrial upgrading, innovation-led growth and greater openness.

A fish swims through clear waters and past green banks, witnessing the patience and rewards of conservation. A kilowatt-hour passes through factories and cities, revealing the pulse of industrial renewal. A microchip travels from laboratory to production line, recording the build-up and breakthroughs of innovation. A shipping container crosses ports and sea routes, charting an ever-wider world of trade.

Each episode stands alone yet echoes the others. Through life, energy, intelligence and the movement of goods, the series reflects the changing Yangtze River Economic Belt.

Blending documentary realism with poetic expression, the series finds the epic in the everyday, allowing a decade of transformation to unfold through a migration, a light switched on, a calculation and a departure.

data.title: Newsom's CPUC Appointees Approve $456 Million PG&E Rate Hike Before Becerra Takes Office, Despite Unanswered Questions About $2 Billion in Spending Cuts, Says Consumer Watchdog
data.description:
Newsom's CPUC Appointees Approve $456 Million PG&E Rate Hike Before Becerra Takes Office, Despite Unanswered Questions About $2 Billion in Spending Cuts, Says Consumer Watchdog

Newsom's CPUC Appointees Approve $456 Million PG&E Rate Hike Before Becerra Takes Office, Despite Unanswered Questions About $2 Billion in Spending Cuts, Says Consumer Watchdog

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Consumer Watchdog criticized Governor Gavin Newsom's appointees to the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) for unanimously approving $456 million in interim rate recovery for Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E). The proceeding, led by Commissioner Matt Baker, moved forward despite unanswered questions about the utility's plans to defer $2 billion in infrastructure investments.

The decision comes just weeks before Governor-elect Xavier Becerra, who has called for a freeze on utility rates to address California's affordability crisis, takes office.

"It is shameful that Newsom's CPUC appointees pushed through another rate increase for PG&E before the incoming governor takes office, without demanding answers about the utility's changing spending plans," said Jamie Court, president of Consumer Watchdog. "The Commission is approving more money for a utility that has already announced it intends to spend billions less than originally planned."

On September 2, PG&E announced it would defer approximately $2 billion in planned 2027 infrastructure investments, including projects affecting electricity connections for approximately 25,000 customers. Yet the CPUC's decision authorizes PG&E to begin collecting an additional $456 million in interim rate recovery on January 1, 2027, before the Commission has completed its review of the utility's General Rate Case.

On October 23, the CPUC's own Public Advocates Office filed a motion warning that PG&E's reduced capital spending made its proposed 2027 revenue requirement overstated and that the Commission should not set rates based on an incomplete evidentiary record.

Consumer Watchdog filed comments urging Commissioner Matthew Baker to withdraw the proposed decision and require PG&E to identify which projects it is deferring before any increase is approved. The group also questioned why PG&E is seeking additional money from customers while reducing its borrowing needs and projecting higher earnings for shareholders.

The Commission's practice of approving interim rate increases before fully examining utilities' costs raises broader concerns about financial accountability and affordability. Although interim collections are subject to refund, customers must pay the higher rates before regulators determine whether the underlying costs are justified.

Consumer Watchdog called for the incoming Becerra administration to bring greater transparency and scrutiny to CPUC decisions, particularly the Commission's practice of granting interim rate increases and its oversight of utility spending.

data.title: CATL Opens Türkiye's First NING SERVICE Experience Center in Istanbul
data.description:
CATL Opens Türkiye's First NING SERVICE Experience Center in Istanbul

CATL Opens Türkiye's First NING SERVICE Experience Center in Istanbul

PR Newswire

ISTANBUL, Türkiye, Nov. 19, 2026

ISTANBUL, Türkiye, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CATL today announced the official launch of its first NING SERVICE Experience Center in Türkiye. The facility serves as the country's first dedicated battery depot repair center and integrated sales-and-service hub, marking a further step in expanding its localized new energy aftermarket service network and supporting the country's shift towards cleaner energy systems.

Türkiye sits at the crossroads of Europe, Asia and the Middle East — a regional economic hub with a fast-growing EV market and a rapidly expanding energy storage sector, where the shift toward clean energy is driving demand for specialized battery support. Its National Energy 2040 plan targets 20 million electric vehicles and 140 GWh of storage requirement by 2040. Against that backdrop, NING SERVICE is delivering full-lifecycle battery services on both the road and the grid, reinforcing the infrastructure that transition depends on.

Located in Istanbul, the NING SERVICE Experience Center represents an important milestone in the collaboration between CATL and Ascendum Türkiye, part of Ascendum Group, offering comprehensive full-lifecycle after-sales support, cultivating local technical talent and accelerating the deployment of advanced electrification and energy storage solutions. 

Covering more than 1,200 square meters, the Istanbul center brings together service zones for battery testing, diagnosis, repair, maintenance and refurbishment, exhibition and retail space, training rooms and a customer lounge. The exhibition and retail area presents CATL's system-level capabilities across electric mobility and energy storage, including bedrock chassis, portable power stations, battery protection plates and integrated charging-and-storage units. The center serves as a localized service hub for the region and as a platform connecting partners across the ecosystem.

Providing a comprehensive new energy aftermarket service system

As CATL's independent aftermarket service brand, NING SERVICE delivers a one-stop, full-lifecycle battery service system that encompass battery diagnostics, repair, maintenance, refurbishment, training, recycling, aftermarket logistics and warehousing. Backed by CATL's deep R&D and extreme manufacturing capabilities, its services product categories from passenger and commercial vehicles to energy storage systems, setting a new benchmark for new energy service delivery in the region.

That capability is delivered through one of the industry's largest after-sales networks:

  • 1,429 professional service locations across more than 80 countries and regions, with the aim of reaching 100 countries and regions by 2027 and 10,000 service locations by 2030;
  • More than 9,900 service engineers and over 10,000 technicians certified for new energy after-sales service, with a 24-hour response mechanism in overseas markets;
  • Its deep-repair capability, delivered through a network of 95 centers, covers 76.8% of EV models and 90% of repair jobs;
  • The Intelligent Eagle Eye System, in use at more than 150 repair facilities, providing full traceability and quality control;
  • The Intelligent Battery Check System, supporting precise battery health diagnostics, slows battery aging by up to 9.5%;
  • More than 70 industry standards participated in or revised, and over 200 authorized patents worldwide

Strengthening local partnerships and service capabilities

CATL is extending its local footprint by strengthening infrastructure and building partnerships in the market. By combining CATL's technological expertise with Ascendum Group's 67 years of industrial heritage and robust local network, the Istanbul center enables CATL to serve clients throughout Türkiye, putting its know-how and rapid-response capability close to where batteries are actually in use.

The center anchors a network to all Türkiye and a team of CATL-certified engineers. It also serves as the network's training base, where technicians are trained and certified to CATL's standards before they work on customer batteries, building a local pool of battery service skills that the market will keep drawing on.

"The opening of Türkiye's first NING SERVICE Experience Center marks an important milestone in our strategic partnership with CATL and represents the first business initiative launched under Ascendum Green.Shift," said Tolga Polat, CEO of Ascendum Türkiye. "By combining CATL's advanced battery technologies with Ascendum's long-standing technical service expertise and customer-focused approach, we aim to provide reliable, high-quality aftermarket solutions across Türkiye. We are investing in local technical capabilities, developing specialized teams and strengthening our service infrastructure to meet the evolving needs of the energy and mobility sectors. Looking ahead, our goal is to gradually expand our service network nationwide and build a sustainable ecosystem that creates long-term value for our customers and supports Türkiye's energy transition."

"Türkiye has moved into the fast lane on electrification, and demand for aftermarket service will grow with it," said Bruce Li, Co-president of Sales & Marketing and President of Commercial Applications & Aftermarket Business of CATL. "As our first NING SERVICE Experience Center in the country, it brings CATL's technology, our training standards and Ascendum's local reach together, so that customers on the road and on the grid are served by people and parts that are already here. From here, we will keep extending our service network across Türkiye, work in step with the country's National Energy 2040 goals, and give the energy transition the service backbone it needs to hold up over time." 

Looking ahead, NING SERVICE will continue to drive innovation in maintenance technology, service models and network expansion. The Istanbul center is the first step in Türkiye, with further network build-out and capability development to follow.

data.title: Stowers Institute appoints Brandon Mayer as Chief Technology Officer
data.description:
Stowers Institute appoints Brandon Mayer as Chief Technology Officer

Stowers Institute appoints Brandon Mayer as Chief Technology Officer

PR Newswire

KANSAS CITY, Mo., Nov. 19, 2026

The veteran technology executive brings more than two decades of experience in digital transformation and enterprise technology, including recent work in artificial intelligence.

KANSAS CITY, Mo., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Stowers Institute for Medical Research has appointed Brandon Mayer as Vice President and Chief Technology Officer. Mayer brings more than two decades of experience leading technology strategy and large-scale organizational transformation.

Mayer most recently served as Chief Information Officer and Chief Transformation Officer at Employers Reassurance Corporation (ERAC), a GE Aerospace company. His expertise spans cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, data analytics, and artificial intelligence.

In his new role, Mayer will lead the Stowers Institute's information technology strategy, research and advanced computing infrastructure, enterprise systems, cybersecurity, and digital transformation initiatives. He will work closely with both scientific leadership and leadership in administrative scientific support. Mayer will report to Kristin Bechard, Stowers Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, to strengthen the technological capabilities that support foundational biological research and enable scientists to manage and analyze increasingly complex data.

"Brandon brings a valuable combination of strategic vision, technical expertise, and experience leading transformation within complex global organizations," said Bechard. "As the opportunities of our scientific research continue to evolve, so must the systems and infrastructure that support it. Brandon's leadership will be instrumental in ensuring our technology investments are thoughtful, secure, and positioned to meet the Institute's needs for years to come."

At ERAC, Mayer led a technology and transformation organization and was responsible for overseeing enterprise applications, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, artificial intelligence platforms and engineering, as well as strategic technology partnerships.

"The Stowers Institute is an extraordinary organization with a mission that places discovery and innovation at its center," said Mayer. "Technology has an increasingly important role to play in enabling scientific progress, from the infrastructure that supports foundational research to the responsible application of AI and advanced data analytics."

During his tenure, Mayer led ERAC's transition from shared corporate technology systems to an independent, cloud-based environment. He also advanced initiatives involving Microsoft Fabric, enterprise analytics, and generative AI, while helping establish governance practices for the responsible use of emerging technologies.

The Institute's distinctive funding model reflects the intent of founders Jim and Virginia Stowers to advance biomedical research for the benefit of human health. Every year, 40% of dividends from American Century Investments support biomedical research at the Stowers Institute, directing more than $2 billion since 2000. This sustained investment enables the Stowers scientists to pursue fundamental biological questions with the potential to inform new approaches to understanding, treating, and preventing disease.

As scientific research generates increasingly large and complex datasets, advances in computational technologies, artificial intelligence, and secure research infrastructure are creating new opportunities to investigate fundamental biological processes.

Mayer added, "I look forward to working with scientists and colleagues across the Institute to build capabilities that support their research while preparing us for the many opportunities ahead."

About the Stowers Institute for Medical Research

Founded in 1994 through the generosity of Jim Stowers, founder of American Century Investments, and his wife, Virginia, the Stowers Institute for Medical Research is a nonprofit biomedical research organization with a focus on foundational research. Its mission is to expand our understanding of the secrets of life and improve life's quality through innovative approaches to the causes, treatment, and prevention of diseases.

The Institute consists of 20 independent research programs. Of the approximately 500 members, more than 370 are scientific staff, including principal investigators, technology center directors, postdoctoral scientists, graduate students, and technical support staff. Learn more at www.stowers.org and www.stowers.org/gradschool.

data.title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. - AADX
data.description:
INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. - AADX

INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. - AADX

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pomerantz LLP is investigating claims on behalf of investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. ("Applied" or the "Company") (NYSE: AADX). Such investors are advised to contact Danielle Peyton at newaction@pomlaw.com or 646-581-9980, ext. 7980.

The investigation concerns whether Applied and certain of its officers and/or directors have engaged in securities fraud or other unlawful business practices. 

[Click here for information about joining the class action]

On or around June 2, 2026, Applied conducted its initial public offering ("IPO"), selling 32.5 million shares of common stock priced at $20.00. Then, on November 11, 2026, Applied reported its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and issued full-year 2026 financial guidance. Despite reporting quarterly revenue growth, Applied lowered its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to a range of $660 million to $670 million—falling below analyst consensus estimates—and projected full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $137 million to $142 million. Management disclosed that supplier constraints in specialized forgings, castings, and fasteners, alongside delayed government regulatory approvals for Apache helicopter rotor head overhauls, had forced the Company to push approximately $15 million to $20 million of high-margin rotorcraft aftermarket revenue out of the fourth quarter of 2026 and into the first half of 2027. Applied also reported that its consolidated gross profit margin compressed to 23.5% from 28.0% in the prior-year period due to program ramp costs and operational inefficiencies, while free cash flow turned negative at -$9.5 million.

On this news, Applied's stock price fell $1.42 per share, or 13.25%, to close at $9.30 per share on November 11, 2026, on heavy trading volume.

Then, on November 16, 2026, Jefferies downgraded Applied from "Buy" to "Hold", citing trimmed 2026 guidance, pushed-out margins, and component delivery delays.

Following the downgrade, Applied's stock price fell $1.57 per share, or 18.74%, to close at $6.81 per share on November 16, 2026.

data.title: Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed Against Fervo Energy Company: The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Outlines Lead Plaintiff Deadline
data.description:
Securities Fraud Lawsuit Filed Against Fervo Energy Company: The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Outlines Lead Plaintiff Deadline

Lawsuit alleges Fervo Energy Company misled investors who acquired its securities on date of IPO, May 13, 2026; lead plaintiff deadline is January 18, 2027

A securities class action lawsuit has been filed against Fervo Energy Company ("Fervo" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: FRVO) on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired ) Class A common stock pursuant and/or traceable to the registration statement and prospectus (collectively, the “Registration Statement”) issued in connection with the Company’s May 13, 2026 initial public offering (“IPO” or the “Offering”). Plaintiff pursues claims under Section 11 and 15 of the Securities Act of 1933 (the "Securities Act"). The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz today reported the case, Nikolov v. Fervo Energy Company, filed on November 19, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas (Case No. 4:26-cv-10141). Lead plaintiff motions in the Fervo Energy Company case are due by January 18, 2027.

If you lost money on Fervo Energy Company investments, contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz to learn more about the Fervo Energy Company class action and your potential claims under the federal securities laws before the January 18, 2027 lead plaintiff deadline.

Fervo Energy Company lawsuit key dates

  • Filed: November 19, 2026
  • Court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas
  • Class period: May 2026 IPO
  • Lead plaintiff motion deadline: January 18, 2027

What happened?

On October 6, 2026, during market hours, Morpheus Research published a report alleging that "Fervo has failed to disclose existential issues related to inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline, excessive water loss, seismicity-related equipment damage, transmission capacity, and ballooning costs. In some cases, Fervo appears to have presented altered data and made material misstatements to investors, including in its [initial public offering] registration statement filed with the [United States Securities and Exchange Commission].”

By the commencement of this action, the Company’s stock price had closed as low as $7.79 per share, a more than 71% decline from the $27 per share IPO price.

What is the Fervo Energy Company class action about?

The Fervo Energy Company securities lawsuit alleges that, throughout the class period, defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts about Fervo Energy Company's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, the complaint alleges defendants failed to disclose to investors that: (1) that Fervo’s pilot plant was experiencing inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline; (2) that Fervo’s EGS operations were experiencing significant injected water loss at a level above the rate the Company’s commercial plans required; (3) that Fervo’s drilling costs were not declining as represented, including as misleadingly represented given previously published data; (4) that Fervo lacked sufficient transmission capacity to deliver power to its California customers as planned, including the transmission path underlying the Company’s approximately 290 MW of rights which was scheduled for retirement before Cape Station Phase II’s targeted 2028 COD; and (5) as a result, defendants' positive statements about Fervo Energy Company's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired Fervo Energy Company securities during the class period may ask the Court, no later than January 18, 2027, to appoint them lead plaintiff in this putative class action.

"According to the complaint filed against Fervo Energy Company, the Company, among other things, failed to disclose that that Fervo’s pilot plant was experiencing inconsistent production temperatures and premature thermal decline. Now that the case has been filed, the January 18, 2027 deadline is the date investors who bought during the class period should know," said Frank R. Cruz of The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz.

What should Fervo Energy Company investors do now?

The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz can help Fervo Energy Company investors evaluate potential claims to recover their losses. To learn more, visit the Fervo Energy Company case page, email info@frankcruzlaw.com, or call 310-914-5007.

If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.

Fervo Energy Company investors need not take any action at this time to be class members. Investors may retain counsel of their choice or take no action and remain absent class members. No class has been certified yet in the Fervo Energy Company case.

Questions and answers about the Fervo Energy Company class action

Who is eligible? Investors who bought Fervo Energy Company securities on May 13, 2026 and lost money may be class members in the Fervo Energy Company securities lawsuit.

What does a lead plaintiff do? The lead plaintiff is appointed by the court to represent all class members and direct the Fervo Energy Company class action, and lead plaintiff motions are due by January 18, 2027.

Must I act now to be part of the Fervo Energy Company class? No, Fervo Energy Company investors need not take any action at this time and may remain absent class members.

How are attorneys' fees handled? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz works on contingency, so investors pay no attorneys' fees unless there is a recovery, and any fees require court approval.
